people.role: Boat Hall disciple; the orphan of the Đào Sa raid
people.appearance: A quiet young man with river-brown skin and a bandolier of black needles ground from old boat nails.
people.backstory: Lữ Tẫn Chu was born in 1166 at Đào Sa Thị, the gold-washers' market where Lãng Đào's ferries landed. His father was a ferryman. In 1173 Lạc Hà's raiders burned the boats at the landing (A080), and his father was on one. The boy spent the next morning fishing nails out of the shallows. A Lạc Hà elder with soot in his beard sat down beside him and helped (N-lac_ha-08). The elder was Lô Xướng Vãn (lo_xuong_van), and he took the boy home to the Boat Hall. Lữ grew up singing the boats' song in the villages of the side that burned his father's boat. He reached Trúc Cơ at thirty-two with needles he had ground from the Đào Sa nails. Lô's grandson Lô Niệm Ca (lo_niem_ca) has never called him brother.
people.wants: To learn who gave the order to burn the landing, and then to decide what he owes them.
people.secret: He has known since he was fifteen that the elder who sat beside him led the raid. He stayed in Lạc Hà to decide whether to forgive Lô Xướng Vãn or kill him. Last year he learned from a Counting House receipt that the order came from the head. On his fifteenth birthday Lô Xướng Vãn showed him ten years of passes stamped with the Nine Bends seal for a toll the pines never set, and that is why he has never answered Giang Cửu Khúc's spring letters, which offer him a boat. This spring he sent one pass down the river inside Giang Tiểu Loan's letters, addressed to Thương Bạch Phàm (thuong_bach_pham).

people.role: Cảnh Trường Thiên's youngest true disciple; walked into the miasma
people.appearance: A tall, rangy woman with her hair cropped short after the miasma burned it, and a grey veil worn loose at the throat.
people.backstory: Hình Lạc Nhạn was born in 1150 in the watch house on the ruin of Vô Định Thành. Her mother was a net-mender from Tân Khẩu Thôn, the harbour the city's refugees founded, where no one speaks of the plain (A182), and she died when her daughter was six. Her father Hình Trọng Sơn (hinh_trong_son) raised her at the Miasma Watch, and she could read the lantern's colour before she could read. Cảnh Trường Thiên (canh_truong_thien) took her as a true disciple in 1170. In 1196 a Tân Khẩu boy walked into the miasma on a dare (A188). She tied on a soaked veil, went three hundred paces in after him and came back with his shoe (N-lac_ha-07). She says she saw a blue gleam in the grey beyond. Her master has forbidden her the plain.
people.wants: To bring Thanh Sương home and put both swords in the head's hands, and to reach Kết Đan before Tô Mộ Vân does.
people.secret: She has promised the lost boy's sister, Đồ Tiểu Liên, that she will go back in. For three years she has been hardening her lungs on Yên Quang's evening-herb tincture to do it.

people.role: Steward of the outer gate at Cựu Hà Viện, the old seat; Tô Mộ Vân's father
people.appearance: A mild, round-faced man with chalk dust on his sleeves from the outer gate's slate boards.
people.backstory: A great-grandson of the head's brother, Tô Bình Chu is a plain steward who will never pass Trúc Cơ, and knows it. When the sect moved in 1185 (N-lac_ha-05) he stayed below to keep the outer gate at the old seat. His daughter Tô Mộ Vân (to_mo_van) is the west's brightest talent. His son Tô Hiểu Chu (to_hieu_chu) is ordinary and on the envoy's list of thirty for Thiên Bảo Trai. He must sign every placement and has signed none. He is offering a poor Hà Khúc family his stipend for ten years if their second child takes his son's place, and he has not told them that the child would be enrolled at the gate only to be sold.

people.role: The head's second disciple; runs the sect's caravans and market stalls
people.appearance: A well-fed man with a merchant's quick smile and three money pouches, one of them always empty.
people.backstory: The head's second disciple, a Hạc Đinh Thị money-changer's son who joined in 1112, Tăng Vân Tiêu runs the sect's caravans and its stalls in four markets. He has stood at the peak of Trúc Cơ for forty years. He spends what he earns on breakthrough pills from Lạc Đan Thanh (lac_dan_thanh), who charges whatever he likes (A186). He likes Hách Ánh Hà, whom he will never outrank. He resents Tô Mộ Vân, who will outrank him within ten years.

people.role: Array runner of the Bridge Hall; tends the galleries under the seat
people.appearance: A small woman with a miner's lamp on a strap round her forehead and dust in every crease of her robe.
people.backstory: A Vân Gian miner's granddaughter whose family went down the mountain in 1040 (V106), Miêu Thạch Lan is Quách Tiếp Vân's (quach_tiep_van) array runner. Each new moon she goes down into the old galleries under the seat to tend the Cloud Bridge Array's lowest nodes. She knows the galleries better than anyone alive. She has noticed that one of them is always locked, and that the head comes out of it with dust on her sleeves.

people.role: The inner gate's best voice; sings the Evening Song at Tử Điện Thành
people.appearance: A slender woman with a clear, carrying voice and a zither always half out of its bag.
people.backstory: Nhiếp Ngọc Âm sings the Evening Song at the bay festivals of Tử Điện Thành. Her mother was born on the Thính Vũ side of the Petal Shore line and still lives there. Since 1188 she has sent the sect's news across the line each month to a soul-vault keeper who serves Lệ Tiêu Hồn (le_tieu_hon), in return for her mother's safety. Her master Sử Thu Thủy (su_thu_thuy) trusts her more than anyone.

people.role: Clerk of the Counting House

people.backstory: A clerk of the Counting House, quick with an abacus and quicker with a contradiction. Phương Toán Ngọc found that the treasury vault has not been opened since 1179: every payment since has come from the trading purse, none from the vault. She took it to her master Tông Thủ Tín (tong_thu_tin), who told her to forget it. She has not.

people.role: Maple Hall disciple; the Wood root the move saved
people.appearance: A gangly man with green-stained nails who talks with his hands and his whole face.
people.backstory: A Wood-heavy lamp-maker's son from Vãn Đăng Thôn, Sài Thanh Phong passed the inner gate by one point of Earth in 1140. On the old seat he reached Trúc Cơ in 1158 and sat at its first stage for thirty years while steppe-born juniors passed him. Three years after the move (N-lac_ha-05) he broke through in a single season. He has become the move's loudest defender, and a bore about it. He writes to Ngạc Viễn Sơn (ngac_vien_son) to say so.

people.appearance: A weathered woman who stands facing the sea whenever she stops walking.
people.backstory: A descendant of Giang Bích Không (giang_bich_khong), Cô Phàm Các's founder, through a grandson who stayed ashore with a fever when the fleet sailed in 705. The family went down to Xích Ngạn with the last watchers of Vọng Phàm Quán (V089). They kept the founder's name and none of his arts. She joined Lạc Hà for Lận Viễn Phàm's (lan_vien_pham) boats. She was meant to sail on both of the boats that were lost, and both times her master took her off at the quay.

people.backstory: Lô Xướng Vãn's (lo_xuong_van) grandson was twenty-four when his mother Lô Tiểu Ca (lo_tieu_ca) fell from the last rope bridge on the Ngư Ca border in 1174 (A202). The year before, his grandfather had brought a ferryman's orphan home from Đào Sa. Lô Niệm Ca believes the boy was taken in to fill his mother's place. He wants the Ferry War fought again and won. He will not sing the ninth verse.

people.backstory: A Hải Yến Trấn nest-picker's daughter (A149) who keeps Lận Viễn Phàm's (lan_vien_pham) charts.
